t: 25.4 g of I₂ and 14.2 g of Cl₂ are made to react completely to yield a mixture of ICl and ICl₃ Calculate moles of ICl and ICl₃ formed
s:
Moles of I₂ = 25.4 g / 254 g/mol = 0.1 mol
Moles of Cl₂ = 14.2 g / 71 g/mol = 0.2 mol

Total moles of I atoms = 2 × 0.1 = 0.2 mol
Total moles of Cl atoms = 2 × 0.2 = 0.4 mol

Let moles of ICl = x and ICl₃ = y.
Applying atom conservation:
For I atoms: x + y = 0.2  ...(1)
For Cl atoms: x + 3y = 0.4 ...(2)

Subtracting (1) from (2):
2y = 0.2 ⇒ y = 0.1 mol (ICl₃)
Substitute y in (1):
x = 0.2 - 0.1 = 0.1 mol (ICl)

Options (B), (C), and (D) violate the conservation of I or Cl atoms.

Correct Answer: (A) 0.1,0.1

t: Calculate the density of an aqueous solution of KI, if its molarity and molality are 1.44M and 1.5 mol kg⁻¹ respectively.
s:
The relation between molality (m), molarity (M), density (d) and molar mass of solute (M_B) is given by:
m=1000M/(1000d−MM_B)
Given data:
Molarity (M) = 1.44 mol L⁻¹
Molality (m) = 1.5 mol kg⁻¹
Molar mass of KI (M_B) = 39+127=166 g mol⁻¹
Substituting these values into the formula:
1.5=(1000×1.44)/(1000×d−1.44×166)
1.5=1440/(1000d−239.04)
1000d−239.04=1440/1.5
1000d−239.04=960
1000d=960+239.04
1000d=1199.04
d=1.19904 g mL⁻¹
Rounding off, d≈1.20 g mL⁻¹

t: 0.5 g of fuming H₂SO₄ (Oleum) is diluted with water. This solution is completely neutralized by 26.7 mL of 0.4 N NaOH. The percentage of free SO₃ in the sample is

t: To 50 mL of 0.1 NNa₂CO₃ solution 150 mL of water is added. What is the molarity of resultant solution?

Final normality (N₂)= To find
and, N₁×V₁=N₂×V₂
0.1×50=(N₂)×200

t: RH₂ (ion exchange resin) can replace Ca²⁺ ions in hard water as: RH₂+Ca²⁺→RCa+2H⁺ If 1 L of hard water after passing through RH₂ has pH=3, then hardness in parts per million of Ca²⁺ is:
s: Given reaction: RH₂+Ca²⁺→RCa+2H⁺ This shows that 1 mole of Ca²⁺ releases 2 moles of H⁺upon ion exchange. Calculate [H⁺]from pH pH=3⇒[H⁺]=10⁻³ mol/L Use stoichiometry to find [ Ca²⁺ ] From the balanced reaction: [Ca²⁺]=([H⁺])/2=10⁻³/2 mol/L Convert to ppm using molar mass of Ca=40g/mol ppm=((40×10⁻³/2)/1)×10⁶=20ppm .

t: If the density of CH₃OH is 0.80 kg L⁻¹, the volume of methanol to prepare 2.5 L of 0.25M aqueous solution is

Mass of CH₃OH required, m₂=n₂M₂=(0.625 mol)(32 g mol⁻¹)=20.0 g=20.0×10⁻³ kg
Volume of CH₃OH required, V=m₂/ρ=(20.0×10⁻³ kg)/(0.80 kg L⁻¹)=0.025 L=25.0 mL

t: The concentration of ethanol in the solution called 86-proof vodka is 6.5M. If the density of the solution is 0.95 g cm⁻³, the amount fraction of ethanol in vodka is

Amount fraction of ethanol, x₂=n₂/(n₁+n₂)=6.5/(36.167+6.5)=0.152

t: If an iron oxide has 69.9 mass % of Fe (molar mass =56.0 g mol⁻¹ ) and 30.1 mass % of oxygen, its molecular formula will be
s:
The iron oxide has 69.9% iron and 30.1% dioxygen by mass.
Thus, 100 g of iron oxide contains 69.9 g iron and 30.1 g dioxygen.
The number of moles of iron present in 100 g of iron oxide are 69.9/55.8=1.25.
The number of moles of dioxygen present in 100 g of iron oxide are 30.1/32= 0.94.
The ratio of the number of oxygen atoms to the number of iron atoms present in one formula unit of iron oxide is (2×0.94)/1.25=1.5:1=3:2.
Hence, the formula of the iron oxide is Fe₂O₃.

t: A mixture of 50.0 g of S and 100.0 gCl₂ reacts of form S₂Cl₂. The mass of S₂Cl₂ formed will be
s:

t: 1.8 g of Mg is burnt in a closed vessel which contains 0.8 g of oxygen. Which of the following statements is not correct? Given ; M(Mg)=24.3 g mol⁻¹.
s:
The reaction is 2Mg+O₂→2MgO
ξₘₐₓ(Mg)=(m_(Mg)/M_(Mg))/(v_(Mg))=(1.8 g/24.3 g mol⁻¹)/2=0.037 mol
ξₘₐₓ(O₂)=(0.8 g/32 g mol⁻¹)/1=0.025 mol
Since ξₘₐₓ(O₂)<ξₘₐₓ(Mg), the limiting reagent is oxygen.
Δn_(MgO)=v_(MgO)ξₘₐₓ(O₂)=2(0.025 mol)=0.05 mol
Mass of Mg consumed =((2M_(Mg))/(M_(O₂)))m_(O₂)=48.6/32×0.8 g=1.22 g
Mass of Mg left behind =1.8 g−1.22 g=0.58 g
o: 0.8 g of Mg is left behind
Oxygen is completely used in the reaction
The extent of reaction at the completion of reaction is 0.025 mol.

t: A solution of acetic acid has molarity equal to 1.35M and molality equal to 1.45 mol kg⁻¹. The density of solution will be
s:
For 1.35M solution, we will have  n₂=1.35 mol  and  V=1000 mL The solution is also 1.45 mol kg⁻¹. The mass of solvent to have 1.35 mol of solute will be
m₁=((1.35 mol)/(1.45 mol kg⁻¹))=0.93103 kg=931.03 g
The mass of solution will be m=m₁+n₂M₂=931.03 g+(1.35 mol)(60 g mol⁻¹)=1012.03 g The density of the solution will be  ρ=m/V=(1012.03 g)/(1000 mL)=1.012 g mL⁻¹

t: The density of a 3 molal solution of sodium thiosulphate (Na₂ S₂O₃⋅5H₂O) solution is 1.25 g cm⁻³. The percentage by mass of sodium thiosulphate is

The mass of solution will be m=m₁+m₂=1000 g+744 g=1744 g
Mass percentage of sodium thiosulphate =m₂/m×100=((744 g)/(1744 g))×100=42.67% .
